title: Turn a prediction into an error
prompt: Implement the squared error for a one-weight model y_hat=w*x. Return a scalar; do not take a square root.

tests.name: Underprediction
tests.reason: The residual is -4, so its square is 16.

tests.name: Exact prediction
tests.reason: A correct prediction has zero error.

tests.name: Overprediction
tests.reason: Positive and negative residuals both cost error.

tests.name: Negative input
tests.reason: Preserve the sign until after subtraction.

hints: Compute prediction and residual as separate local variables.
Square the residual, not the prediction.
explanation: This objective scores one numerical prediction. A language model later uses a different loss, but still separates prediction from evaluation.
transfer: Derive the derivative with respect to w without changing the function signature.

title: Build next-token training targets
prompt: Return every token except the first. Empty input and a single token produce an empty result. This is the target half of one shifted training sequence.

tests.name: Three prediction targets
tests.reason: The target is one position ahead, not a sorted sequence.

tests.name: One token
tests.reason: One token provides no next-token pair.

tests.name: Empty text
tests.reason: Avoid constructing an invalid iterator.

tests.name: Repeated IDs
tests.reason: Duplicates carry meaningful positions.

hints: The output length is max(0,N-1).
Never reorder or deduplicate the IDs.
explanation: Teacher forcing obtains targets from the original text. A training sample still needs the matching input prefix.
transfer: Return both input and target arrays, then add document-boundary handling.

title: Budget more than the weights
prompt: Estimate bytes for float32 weights, gradients, and two Adam moments. There are four arrays, each with P elements of 4 bytes. Exclude activations and allocator overhead explicitly.

tests.name: One million parameters
tests.reason: Weights alone use 4 MB; this estimate uses four arrays.

tests.name: Single parameter
tests.reason: Check the per-parameter unit.

tests.name: Empty model
tests.reason: Zero parameters need zero parameter-state bytes.

hints: Write the units: parameters × arrays × bytes/element.
This does not include activations.
explanation: A 16 MB estimate for one million parameters is a lower-level accounting fixture, not a promise that the entire run uses only 16 MB.
transfer: Convert your result to GiB and add an independently measured activation budget.

title: Write the weighted sum
prompt: Compute a dot product. Equal-sized input vectors are guaranteed; define the empty product as zero. Your implementation must handle negative values.

tests.name: Two-dimensional vectors
tests.reason: Multiply matching coordinates, then add.

tests.name: Negative coordinate
tests.reason: The negative contribution is -2.

tests.name: Empty vectors
tests.reason: The accumulator starts at zero.

tests.name: Orthogonal vectors
tests.reason: Different active coordinates give zero alignment.

hints: Initialize an accumulator to 0.0.
Elementwise multiplication returns a vector; dot returns one number.
explanation: A linear neuron uses this weighted sum before adding its bias and nonlinearity.
transfer: Add dimension validation to your local C++ version, where exceptions are supported.

title: Reject an impossible matrix product
prompt: Return true exactly when A(m,k) and B(r,n) can be multiplied. All dimensions must be positive, and A columns must equal B rows.

tests.name: Rectangular valid shapes
tests.reason: The shared reduction dimension is 3.

tests.name: Inner mismatch
tests.reason: Equal outer dimensions do not rescue a mismatch.

tests.name: Zero dimension policy
tests.reason: This exercise explicitly rejects empty axes.

tests.name: Negative dimension
tests.reason: Dimensions cannot be negative.

hints: The inner axes must agree.
Check all four positivity conditions, not just the two inner dimensions.
explanation: This is a shape contract for our small engine; some mature tensor libraries allow empty axes with different semantics.
transfer: Compute the output shape and approximate 2mkn arithmetic work for a valid product.

title: Differentiate through two operations
prompt: Return dL/dx for u=2x+1 and L=u². Derive this by multiplying the two local derivatives.

tests.name: Positive x
tests.reason: dL/du=14 and du/dx=2.

tests.name: At x=0
tests.reason: A zero input does not imply a zero derivative.

tests.name: At the minimum
tests.reason: The squared inner value is minimized here.

tests.name: Negative x
tests.reason: Gradients can point toward increasing x.

hints: Differentiate the square with respect to u first.
Multiply by du/dx; do not add the two derivatives.
explanation: The numerical value of the loss and its derivative are different quantities. Local derivatives multiply along each graph path.
transfer: Compare your derivative with centered differences at x=0.7.

title: Score target probability
prompt: Return negative natural log probability. Inputs are valid probabilities in (0,1]. Use std::log.

tests.name: Likely target
tests.reason: Natural logarithms measure loss in nats.

tests.name: Certain target
tests.reason: Correct certainty costs zero.

tests.name: Unlikely target
tests.reason: Low target probability should cost more.

tests.name: Ordering
tests.reason: Loss rewards probability on the actual target.

hints: C++ std::log is the natural logarithm.
The result must be nonnegative for these inputs.
explanation: Cross-entropy for a one-hot target selects the negative log probability of that target.
transfer: Add an explicit input-validity contract in the local lab.

title: Make one descent step
prompt: For L=(w-3)², return w after one gradient-descent step with learning rate eta. Do not update eta.

tests.name: First descent step
tests.reason: The initial derivative is -6, so subtracting it moves right.

tests.name: From the other side
tests.reason: A positive derivative decreases the weight.

tests.name: Stationary point
tests.reason: The gradient at the minimum is zero.

tests.name: Large-step oscillation
tests.reason: Eta=1 overshoots without reducing distance.

tests.name: Zero rate
tests.reason: No learning rate means no update.

hints: The derivative is 2*(w-3).
A minus sign in the optimizer can multiply a negative gradient.
explanation: Correct update direction is foundational. The test at eta=1 checks the mathematics, not whether this is a good rate.
transfer: Iterate 50 times and compare eta=.1,1,1.1 in the playground.

title: Average a regression gradient
prompt: Return the gradient with respect to w of mean squared error for y_hat=w*x+b. x and y have equal nonzero sizes.

tests.name: Worked initial gradient
tests.reason: The two residual-weighted terms sum to -26 and average to -13.

tests.name: Exact fit
tests.reason: An exact linear fit has zero residuals.

tests.name: Repeated data invariant
tests.reason: A mean objective is invariant to duplicating every example.

tests.name: Bias included
tests.reason: The prediction includes b before forming the residual.

hints: For one example the derivative is 2*(prediction-target)*x.
Divide by N once, outside the loop.
explanation: The duplicated-data fixture catches a missing mean reduction.
transfer: Implement the bias derivative and verify both with finite differences.

title: Keep classification loss finite
prompt: Implement stable binary cross-entropy from logit z and target y∈{0,1}: max(z,0)-z*y+log1p(exp(-abs(z))).

tests.name: Uncertain prediction
tests.reason: Zero logits assign equal probabilities.

tests.name: Confident correct
tests.reason: The stable formula avoids exp(1000).

tests.name: Confident incorrect
tests.reason: Wrong confidence must carry a large finite penalty.

tests.name: Negative correct
tests.reason: Stability must hold on both sides.

hints: Do not compute log(sigmoid(z)) directly.
std::log1p improves log(1+x) when x is small.
explanation: Stable algebra preserves the intended objective even at extreme logits.
transfer: Derive and implement dL/dz=sigmoid(z)-y.

title: Do not drop the final batch
prompt: Return the number of updates for n examples with batch size b. Inputs satisfy n≥0,b>0. Include a final partial batch.

tests.name: Partial last batch
tests.reason: The groups are 4,4,2.

tests.name: Exact fit
tests.reason: No extra empty batch should be created.

tests.name: Tiny dataset
tests.reason: A nonempty partial batch still updates.

tests.name: Empty dataset
tests.reason: No examples means no updates.

hints: Integer division alone rounds down.
A nonzero remainder needs one additional batch.
explanation: Dropping or misnormalizing the final batch changes the training algorithm.
transfer: Return the actual size of each batch and verify the sum is n.

title: Audit document-level separation
prompt: Return true when no source ID appears in both train and evaluation. Duplicate IDs within one side are allowed.

tests.name: Independent documents
tests.reason: No source document is reused.

tests.name: Leaked document
tests.reason: Shared ID 2 contaminates the assessment.

tests.name: Duplicates within training
tests.reason: Repeating an ID on one side is not cross-split overlap.

tests.name: Empty training side
tests.reason: The empty set has no overlap.

hints: Compare source IDs, not positions within a token window.
Return early only when you find overlap.
explanation: This quadratic implementation is deliberately small. A production audit should use a hash set and source provenance.
transfer: Group paraphrase families before splitting your specialized assistant dataset.

title: Compute one nonlinear neuron
prompt: Compute tanh(w·x+b). Equal-sized x and w are guaranteed. Accumulate all inputs before applying tanh.

tests.name: Worked neuron
tests.reason: The preactivation is 1.

tests.name: Bias only
tests.reason: The affine sum starts with the bias.

tests.name: Negative activation
tests.reason: Tanh preserves the sign of the preactivation.

tests.name: Cancellation
tests.reason: Apply tanh after summation.

hints: Initialize z with b.
Moving tanh inside the sum computes a different model.
explanation: The nonlinearity prevents a stack of layers from collapsing into one affine map.
transfer: Compute its derivative with respect to each weight using 1-tanh²(z).

title: Accumulate both graph paths
prompt: For u=x*x and L=u+u, return dL/dx. Work backward: u receives two contributions; multiplication uses x on both edges.

tests.name: Shared positive node
tests.reason: Four local path contributions combine.

tests.name: Negative input
tests.reason: The gradient sign follows x.

tests.name: Zero point
tests.reason: Both multiplication paths contribute zero here.

tests.name: Fractional input
tests.reason: Do not assume integer-only graph values.

hints: L=2x² is a useful independent simplification.
A graph traversal visits nodes once, but the backward rule must preserve duplicate edges.
explanation: Using assignment instead of += silently loses paths in an autodiff engine.
transfer: Implement this graph in your arena-based tape and compare against this scalar oracle.

title: Compare analytic and numerical derivatives
prompt: Return abs(a-b)/max(1e-8,abs(a)+abs(b)). This relative error complements an absolute error near zero gradients.

tests.name: Equal gradients
tests.reason: Exact agreement has zero error.

tests.name: Opposite directions
tests.reason: Opposite signs must not cancel the denominator.

tests.name: Near zero
tests.reason: The denominator floor prevents division by zero.

tests.name: Both zero
tests.reason: The result must remain finite.

hints: Use |a|+|b|, not |a+b|.
The floor is inside max.
explanation: A relative error by itself is not reliable for tiny gradients. Record both error measures and use smooth fixtures.
transfer: Write a centered-difference checker for every parameter of a two-neuron network.

title: Update every parameter exactly once
prompt: Return a new parameter vector equal to p-eta*g. p and g are equal-sized. Do not mutate your input vectors.

tests.name: Two parameters
tests.reason: Negative gradients increase their corresponding parameter.

tests.name: Zero rate
tests.reason: Eta zero leaves all parameters fixed.

tests.name: Empty model
tests.reason: The function handles no parameters.

tests.name: Zero gradient
tests.reason: A zero gradient makes no update.

hints: Copy p before changing the output.
Use the same coordinate index for p and g.
explanation: The optimizer updates parameters after backward; it does not compute the gradients.
transfer: Add a training loop that clears gradients and rebuilds the forward graph each step.

title: Map an index into row-major storage
prompt: Return the flat offset for shape [2,3,4]. Indices are valid. The contiguous strides are [12,4,1].

tests.name: Last element
tests.reason: The last logical coordinate maps to the last of 24 elements.

tests.name: Origin
tests.reason: Storage starts at zero.

tests.name: Next row
tests.reason: Advancing the middle axis skips four scalars.

tests.name: Next outer slice
tests.reason: One outer slice contains 3×4 elements.

hints: The last axis has stride 1.
An axis stride is the product of the later dimensions.
explanation: Shape and stride determine addressing; bounds checks are a separate contract.
transfer: Generalize to arbitrary dimensions and reject each out-of-bounds axis before computing offsets.

title: Undo broadcasting by summing
prompt: A bias vector is broadcast across a B×H matrix. Return its gradient by summing upstream rows. Inputs are flattened row-major and have B*H entries.

tests.name: Two rows of ones
tests.reason: Each bias was used in two rows.

tests.name: Different contributions
tests.reason: Reduce along B, not along H.

tests.name: Negative cancellation
tests.reason: Contributions can cancel.

tests.name: Empty batch
tests.reason: No uses mean zero gradient.

hints: Initialize H outputs to zero.
Forward reuse becomes backward accumulation.
explanation: Do not divide by B here: any mean-loss scaling must already be in the upstream derivative.
transfer: Add a finite-difference test for a bias added to two matrix rows.

title: Implement a rectangular matrix product
prompt: Compute row-major A(M,K)B(K,N). Shapes and storage sizes are valid; return M*N elements. Start with three loops before optimizing.

tests.name: Worked product
tests.reason: Each result is a row-column dot product.

tests.name: Rectangular fixture
tests.reason: N and K are different, exposing a wrong stride.

tests.name: Identity
tests.reason: Multiplication by identity preserves a row.

tests.name: Negative products
tests.reason: Signed values still follow scalar multiplication.

hints: A index is i*K+k; B index is k*N+j.
C uses the output width N as its row stride.
explanation: These dimensions recur in embeddings, projections, and attention. Correctness comes before blocking or SIMD.
transfer: Implement dA=dC Bᵀ and dB=Aᵀ dC and gradient-check them.

title: Normalize extreme logits safely
prompt: Return softmax probabilities for a nonempty vector of finite logits. Subtract the maximum before exponentiating.

tests.name: Large logits
tests.reason: Direct exp(1001) overflows.

tests.name: Equal logits
tests.reason: Equal scores split mass uniformly.

tests.name: Shift invariance
tests.reason: A shared additive constant cancels.

tests.name: Single class
tests.reason: All probability belongs to the only class.

hints: At least one shifted exponential equals 1.
Divide each exponential by the sum, not by the maximum.
explanation: This is real stable normalization, not clipping a broken result. For cross-entropy prefer log-sum-exp directly.
transfer: Add target cross-entropy and verify its logit gradients sum to zero.

title: Reject an incompatible checkpoint header
prompt: Validate our toy checkpoint metadata: version must be 1, stored parameter count must equal expected, and the tokenizer ID must match exactly. This checks metadata, not file contents.

tests.name: Matching metadata
tests.reason: All contract fields agree.

tests.name: Newer version
tests.reason: Do not silently interpret an unsupported format.

tests.name: Wrong tokenizer
tests.reason: Matching shapes do not guarantee the same token semantics.

tests.name: Truncated parameter count
tests.reason: Missing weights cannot be accepted.

hints: Use conjunction: every condition must hold.
A tokenizer mismatch matters even with identical parameter counts.
explanation: A complete checkpoint reader must also validate lengths, shapes, dtypes, data integrity, and optimizer state.
transfer: Implement a file round trip locally and reject a physically truncated file.

title: Count UTF-8 code points
prompt: For valid UTF-8 input only, count bytes that are not continuation bytes. This counts Unicode code points, not user-perceived graphemes.

tests.name: ASCII
tests.reason: Each ASCII byte starts a code point.

tests.name: Accented character
tests.reason: The second UTF-8 byte is a continuation.

tests.name: Four-byte emoji
tests.reason: One code point can use four bytes.

tests.name: Combining sequence
tests.reason: One visible accented grapheme can contain two code points.

tests.name: Empty input
tests.reason: No bytes means no code points.

hints: Use unsigned char when inspecting byte bits.
(c & 0xC0) == 0x80 identifies a continuation byte.
explanation: This exercise assumes valid UTF-8; it is not a decoder or an input-validity checker.
transfer: Compare byte, code-point, and grapheme counts in the tokenization explorer.

title: Give unseen transitions a probability
prompt: Return add-alpha-smoothed probability of count c in a row with total transitions total and vocabulary V. Assume alpha>0,V>0.

tests.name: Seen transition
tests.reason: Counts [2,0] become [3,1].

tests.name: Unseen transition
tests.reason: Smoothing avoids log(0).

tests.name: Empty row
tests.reason: An unseen row becomes uniform.

tests.name: Fractional smoothing
tests.reason: Alpha is not restricted to integer counts.

hints: Every vocabulary entry receives alpha mass.
Normalizing only by total+alpha is incorrect for V>1.
explanation: A count model is an explicit baseline your neural model should improve on.
transfer: Compute held-out mean negative log likelihood without changing the counts.

title: Accumulate repeated embedding IDs
prompt: Given token IDs and one scalar upstream gradient per occurrence, return the gradient for a V×1 embedding table. IDs are valid and arrays have equal size.

tests.name: Repeated token
tests.reason: ID 1 receives both occurrence gradients.

tests.name: Unused rows
tests.reason: Rows not looked up remain zero.

tests.name: Cancellation
tests.reason: The backward operation sums signed contributions.

tests.name: Empty sequence
tests.reason: No lookups give a zero table.

hints: Allocate V zeros.
Use += because multiple positions share one parameter row.
explanation: This scalar-column fixture isolates scatter-add; real embeddings also loop across C channels.
transfer: Generalize to V×C and add tied input/output embedding contributions.

title: Perform one non-overlapping BPE merge
prompt: Replace every left-to-right adjacent pair (a,b) with merged. Do one pass; newly merged IDs are not reconsidered.

tests.name: Repeated pair
tests.reason: Both non-overlapping occurrences merge.

tests.name: Overlapping candidates
tests.reason: The middle ID cannot belong to two merges.

tests.name: Unmatched end
tests.reason: Do not access past the final ID.

tests.name: Empty input
tests.reason: The pass must terminate on empty text.

hints: Use a while-style loop with an explicit index increment.
On a match advance by 2.
explanation: Learning pair rankings and applying ranked merges are separate parts of a full BPE tokenizer.
transfer: Implement pair-frequency counting and a reversible merge vocabulary.

title: Mask before normalizing attention
prompt: Given one row of finite attention scores, return a probability vector of the same length with positions >query equal to zero. query is a valid zero-based index.

tests.name: First token sees itself
tests.reason: Future scores cannot influence the visible distribution.

tests.name: Uniform visible prefix
tests.reason: Masked scores are excluded from the denominator.

tests.name: Stable large scores
tests.reason: Subtract the maximum over only visible scores.

tests.name: Last position
tests.reason: The last query may see all three keys.

hints: Never let a future score enter max or sum.
Initialize all outputs to zero, then fill the visible prefix.
explanation: Masking after a full softmax without renormalization is not equivalent to causal attention.
transfer: Multiply the resulting row by scalar values and test future-value invariance.

title: Rotate a query pair
prompt: Return a 2D rotation of (x,y) by theta radians. This is the paired-coordinate arithmetic used inside RoPE.

tests.name: Quarter turn
tests.reason: The positive x axis rotates onto positive y.

tests.name: Zero angle
tests.reason: Identity rotation preserves coordinates.

tests.name: Negative angle
tests.reason: The sine term must keep its sign.

tests.name: Half turn
tests.reason: A half turn flips both coordinates.

hints: Use radians, not degrees.
The x output has a minus sine term; y has a plus sine term.
explanation: Full RoPE selects an angle for every position and coordinate pair, then rotates both queries and keys.
transfer: Apply a rotation and its inverse, and numerically test norm preservation.

title: Normalize by root mean square
prompt: Return x/sqrt(mean(x²)+epsilon). Input is nonempty, epsilon>0, and learned gains are omitted in this small fixture.

tests.name: Two features
tests.reason: The denominator uses (9+16)/2.

tests.name: Zero input
tests.reason: Epsilon keeps zero inputs finite.

tests.name: Signed features
tests.reason: Normalization preserves signs.

tests.name: Constant vector
tests.reason: RMSNorm does not subtract the mean.

hints: RMS is not the standard deviation.
Add epsilon inside the square root.
explanation: The constant-vector test distinguishes RMSNorm from centered LayerNorm.
transfer: Add learned channel gains and gradient-check a small vector.

title: Cover a GPU dispatch safely
prompt: Return ceiling(n/threads_per_group) for n≥0, group size>0. The final group may contain padding threads, so a real kernel still needs tid<n.

tests.name: Boundary padding
tests.reason: Four groups cover only 256 elements.

tests.name: Exact division
tests.reason: Do not create an unnecessary group.

tests.name: Single element
tests.reason: One element still needs a group.

tests.name: No elements
tests.reason: The host can skip an empty dispatch.

hints: Integer division truncates.
Ceiling group count does not remove the kernel bounds check.
explanation: This CPU drill checks launch arithmetic only. A browser WASI program cannot execute Metal kernels.
transfer: Use this result in your local Metal host and compare n=257 with CPU output.

title: Compare CPU and GPU results honestly
prompt: Return true if |a-b| ≤ atol+rtol*|reference|. Use b as the reference. Both tolerances are nonnegative and inputs are finite.

tests.name: Near zero
tests.reason: Absolute tolerance matters near zero.

tests.name: Large magnitude
tests.reason: A small relative discrepancy can be acceptable.

tests.name: Wrong result
tests.reason: Tolerance must not accept arbitrary errors.

tests.name: Negative reference
tests.reason: Reference magnitude needs abs.

hints: Subtract the two outputs before taking abs.
The relative term uses absolute reference magnitude.
explanation: Passing tolerances is a numerical agreement claim, not a performance claim. Choose tolerances appropriate to dtype and operation.
transfer: Report maximum absolute error and relative error on nonsquare CPU/GPU fixtures.

title: Clip a global gradient norm
prompt: Return g scaled to have norm at most limit. If g has zero norm, return it unchanged. Assume limit>0.

tests.name: 3-4-5 vector
tests.reason: Global clipping preserves direction.

tests.name: Already small
tests.reason: Do not enlarge a small gradient.

tests.name: Zero norm
tests.reason: Avoid dividing by zero.

tests.name: Negative direction
tests.reason: The shared scale is positive.

hints: Compute sqrt(sum(g_i²)).
Clip the norm, not individual coordinates.
explanation: This is global norm clipping; it differs from componentwise clipping. Apply before the optimizer update.
transfer: Extend your local AdamW loop and record unclipped and clipped norms.

title: Account for quadratic attention storage
prompt: Return bytes for a materialized float32 score tensor [B,H,T,T]. Inputs are small nonnegative values; compute in double to avoid intermediate integer overflow.

tests.name: Context doubled
tests.reason: Doubling T quadruples the score storage.

tests.name: Batch scales linearly
tests.reason: The batch axis appears once.

tests.name: Empty context
tests.reason: Zero positions produce no scores.

hints: T appears twice.
Weights and KV-cache bytes are separate allocations.
explanation: Efficient attention can avoid storing this full tensor; the formula is for the naive materialized implementation.
transfer: Compare measured memory with this estimate and list additional allocations.

title: Serialize a toy conversation boundary
prompt: Our explicitly toy format is <user>MESSAGE</user><assistant>. Return that exact sequence. Assume message contains no reserved markers. Real models require their own actual templates.

tests.name: Simple message
tests.reason: The assistant generation boundary must be present.

tests.name: Preserve whitespace
tests.reason: Do not silently retokenize the message.

tests.name: Empty message
tests.reason: An empty message still has structural boundaries.

hints: This is string serialization, not an inference call.
The example format is a teaching contract, not a universal chat template.
explanation: Correct template serialization preserves role and generation boundaries. This fixture does not emulate a trained assistant.
transfer: Render the actual template of your selected local model and compare token IDs.

title: Apply a low-rank weight update
prompt: For a rank-one update ΔW=B A with B shaped [M,1] and A [1,N], return row-major ΔW. This is a simple outer product.

tests.name: Rectangular outer product
tests.reason: The output keeps M and N, reducing the rank axis.

tests.name: Negative update
tests.reason: Adapter updates are signed.

tests.name: Zero factor
tests.reason: A zero factor produces zero update.

hints: The rank axis has one element, so there is no visible inner sum.
General rank r adds a sum over r.
explanation: Ordinary LoRA learns small factors while base weights remain frozen. A complete adapter includes scaling and selected target layers.
transfer: Add general rank r and compare parameter counts with a dense update.

title: Score correctness, not fluency
prompt: Return the fraction of exactly matching predicted and expected rule IDs. Equal nonempty lengths are guaranteed. Return a floating-point fraction.

tests.name: Partial correctness
tests.reason: Three of four labels match.

tests.name: No correct outputs
tests.reason: Plausible-looking wrong labels still fail.

tests.name: All correct
tests.reason: Report a fraction from zero to one.

tests.name: Avoid integer division
tests.reason: The numerator must convert before division.

hints: Count exact matches on frozen held-out tasks.
Integer division truncates partial accuracy to zero.
explanation: This fixture checks exact-match accounting only. Real rules also need syntax, domain, and semantic validation.
transfer: Report per-category raw counts and compare all baselines on the same held-out cases.

title: Interpret an exact threshold rule
prompt: Our rule language supports >=, >, and ==. Return whether x satisfies op threshold. Unknown operators must return false.

tests.name: Inclusive boundary
tests.reason: At least 18 includes exactly 18.

tests.name: Strict boundary
tests.reason: Over 18 excludes exactly 18.

tests.name: Above boundary
tests.reason: Strict inequality accepts a higher value.

tests.name: Equality
tests.reason: Equality is part of the declared vocabulary.

tests.name: Unknown operator
tests.reason: Unsupported semantics must not be invented.

hints: Test the exact boundary, not only points far away.
An unknown operator must have an explicit failure behavior.
explanation: A model-generated rule only becomes usable when its semantics are interpreted and tested precisely.
transfer: Generate boundary triplets threshold-1, threshold, threshold+1 for every numeric rule.

title: Bound verifier-guided retries
prompt: Return the zero-based index of the first valid proposal among at most budget proposals, or -1 if none is valid. budget≥0.

tests.name: Accept second proposal
tests.reason: Return the first valid candidate.

tests.name: Budget exhaustion
tests.reason: A later valid candidate is outside the budget.

tests.name: No attempts
tests.reason: Zero budget cannot accept a proposal.

tests.name: No proposals
tests.reason: Do not read beyond the available candidates.

hints: Use both loop bounds.
Failure must be explicit, not the final invalid proposal.
explanation: A retry loop is only as sound as its verifier. This policy controls cost and makes failure observable.
transfer: Add rejection reasons and include retry cost in your assistant latency report.

title: Measure an ablation honestly
prompt: Return full_score-ablated_score. Preserve the sign so a harmful component has a negative contribution. Scores use the same metric and held-out set.

tests.name: Helpful component
tests.reason: The component adds 0.2 to the score.

tests.name: Harmful component
tests.reason: Do not take an absolute value.

tests.name: No measured change
tests.reason: A zero delta is still an informative result.

hints: Metric direction matters: this function assumes higher is better.
Loss reduction would use a different sign convention.
explanation: A score difference is not causal evidence unless the runs control confounding changes. Raw counts and uncertainty still matter.
transfer: Run matched-budget baselines, freeze the evaluation set, and document one negative result.
